steps.message:
Six depots export their shipments to /app/data, each in its own format. Write a Python script at /app/bin/summarize.py that builds the shipment summary described in /app/docs/summary-format.md, run it on /app/data, and save its output as /app/out/summary.json. The script will also be run on other exports from the same depots, so it must work from the files it is given rather than from what the current files contain.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

# Shipment summary

## Script

`/app/bin/summarize.py` is run as

    python3 /app/bin/summarize.py DATA_DIR OUT_FILE

It reads every export in `DATA_DIR`, writes the summary as JSON to `OUT_FILE`
and exits with status 0. Python 3.12 standard library only. The script is also
run on other exports from the same depots, so nothing about the current
contents of `/app/data` may be built into it.

## Output

```json
{
  "depots": {
    "<depot>": {"shipments": 0, "total_kg": 0.0}
  },
  "by_month": {"YYYY-MM": 0},
  "duplicates_resolved": 0
}
```

- `depots` has one entry per export file in `DATA_DIR`. The depot name is the
  file name without its extension. A depot with no counted shipments still has
  an entry with zeros.
- `shipments` is the number of counted shipments credited to the depot.
- `total_kg` is the sum of their weights in kilograms. Convert each weight
  exactly, add them up, and round the sum to 2 decimals.
- `by_month` maps each month that has at least one counted shipment to the
  number of counted shipments shipped in that month, over all depots. Keys are
  in ascending order.
- `duplicates_resolved` is defined in `duplicates.md`.

## Records

- Every data record in an export is one shipment. Comment lines, column
  headers, totals and trailer records are not shipments.
- A shipment id is the letters SH followed by a number. Exports format ids
  differently (prefix case, separators, zero padding). Two records refer to the
  same shipment when their numbers are equal. See `duplicates.md`.
- A shipment is counted when its status is `delivered` or `delivered_late`,
  compared without regard to case and with spaces and hyphens read as
  underscores. Every other status (cancelled, returned, held, and so on) is not
  counted.
- Each export states its weight unit and its date convention in the file
  itself: in a header comment, a column or field name, an attribute, or the
  layout it names. Conversions: 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg, 1 oz = 0.028349523125 kg,
  1 g = 0.001 kg.
- The month of a shipment is the calendar month of its ship time in UTC. A ship
  date without a time of day is already a UTC date.
- A fixed-width export names its layout on its first line, as `#LAYOUT <name>`.
  The layout is described in `/app/docs/layouts/<name>.txt`. Depots move between
  layouts from one export to the next, so the script must follow the layout the
  file names.

## Checking

`python3 /app/tools/check_summary.py` checks the shape of `/app/out/summary.json`
and that it matches what the script produces. It stops at the first problem it
finds. It does not check the values.

# Duplicate shipments

A parcel that is handed over between depots is exported by both of them. The
two records describe the same shipment, but they can disagree on weight, date
and status, because each depot records what it saw.

When the same shipment number appears in more than one export, keep exactly one
record: the one from the export that comes first in this order.

1. central
2. south
3. east
4. river
5. north
6. west

Every other record of that shipment is dropped. The kept record alone decides
the depot the shipment is credited to, its weight, its month and whether it is
counted. If the kept record is not counted (for example, it is cancelled), the
shipment is not counted at all, even when a dropped record says delivered.

`duplicates_resolved` is the number of shipment numbers that appear in more
than one export, whatever the status of their records.
== docs/layouts/FW1.txt
Fixed-width shipment layout FW1

Columns are 1-based and inclusive. Fields are padded with spaces on the right
or zeros on the left.

  id        1-9    shipment id
  shipped   10-16  ship date as YYYYDDD (year, then day of the year 001-366)
  weight    17-24  weight in grams, integer
  status    25-25  status code
  note      26-41  free text, ignored

Status codes:

  D  delivered
  L  delivered late
  C  cancelled
  R  returned
  H  held at depot

Lines starting with # are not shipments. The last line is #END followed by the
number of shipment lines.
== docs/layouts/FW2.txt
Fixed-width shipment layout FW2

Replaces FW1. Columns are 1-based and inclusive. Fields are padded with spaces
on the right or zeros on the left.

  id        1-9    shipment id
  status    10-10  status code
  shipped   11-17  ship date as YYYYDDD (year, then day of the year 001-366)
  weight    18-24  weight in hundredths of a kilogram, integer (0001250 = 12.50 kg)
  note      25-40  free text, ignored

Status codes are the same as in FW1:

  D  delivered
  L  delivered late
  C  cancelled
  R  returned
  H  held at depot

Lines starting with # are not shipments. The last line is #END followed by the
number of shipment lines.

A parcel that is handed over between depots is exported by both of them. The
two records describe the same shipment, but they can disagree on weight, date
and status, because each depot records what it saw.

When the same shipment number appears in more than one export, keep exactly one
record: the one from the export that comes first in this order.

1. central

4. river
5. north
6. west

Every other record of that shipment is dropped. The kept record alone decides
the depot the shipment is credited to, its weight, its month and whether it is
counted. If the kept record is not counted (for example, it is cancelled), the
shipment is not counted at all, even when a dropped record says delivered.

`duplicates_resolved` is the number of shipment numbers that appear in more
than one export, whatever the status of their records.
